en: Hm? You smell something?
It's a gas leak! Open the windows!
Sorry to bug you with all these questions, Uno-san.
It's fine. Now I can visit the new girl.
Huh? Hey, Shinada. You forgot your phone.
Uno-san?
I remembered something... Was it because of that phone?
Huh? Something happen with a phone?
I told you, right? How I got canned out of nowhere fifteen years ago?
Just like now, a player forgot his phone in the massage room. So I took it to him.
Yeah? Whose was it?
That was, uh, let's see... Manabe! It was Manabe's phone.
Oh, Manabe-san?
Manabe? As in the Wyverns' former cleanup hitter? That Manabe?
Yeah. The guy nearly went berserk over losing that phone.
Hm? Who left this here?

That day, I found a phone in my massage room. So I hurried
to the locker room, and then I heard the uproar...
Where's my goddamn phone!? I know I had it on me! Who took it!?
Uh, Manabe-san, could this be it?
The hell!? Why do you have it!? Huh!?
Then he snatched his phone out of my hand and began checking it all frantic.
Uh, Manabe-san? I think I deserve a thanks, at least.
Hey, Manabe-san?
You didn't go rootin' through my texts, did ya?
The way Manabe looked then... He wasn't right in the head.
What was on his phone?

Hard to say. I didn't own a cell phone at the time, so I
couldn't have known how to check one even if I wanted to.
But now that it's all coming back to me, Manabe's behavior was definitely off.
Maybe that phone had something to do with the match fixing? Like he was getting instructions through text?
It's possible. Maybe he thought you saw something not meant for your eyes, and that's what got you fired out of the blue.
Okay. So that's what happened...
I guess we need to check on Manabe-san, then. You know what he's up to these days?
Didn't he retire around five years back?
Yeah, he tried his hand at running a few businesses, but they all went tits up. Only thing left is a little yakiniku place in Karibacho.
A yakiniku place, huh...
I went to eat there once and he kicked me right out. Come to think of it, that's even more suspicious.
Then we're off to this yakiniku place of his. Thanks.
Welcome to⑬ Eh?
It's you?
Hey, I'm a paying customer.
Using that seedy loan shark's money?
That seedy loan shark has feelings, y'know.
Come on, Uno-san. Do it for old times' sake.
Then lie your ass down.
It's been a long fifteen years since I last treated you.
This is the first massage I've had since my baseball days, other than the sexy kind.
Wouldn't want anyone else messing up my muscles.
That's music to a trainer's ears.
Uno-san... Why'd you quit working with the team?

I can't think of anyone out there that's as good as you.
The team must've begged you to stay.

Well, it was nice touring titty bars across Japan with the
team, but remember how we all woke up at the crack of dawn?
I never got off in time for the early morning discount. So in the end, this worked out better for me.
Come on, that seriously can't be it.
Heh. I was canned, just like you.
Fifteen years ago. Almost the same time you got the boot.
They told me they found a better trainer for the team and fired me over the phone.
They renewed my contract before the year started, so I should've been with them for the season at least. But they let me go right after.
I never knew...
We've never talked about it.

Once our dreams of baseball came screeching to a halt,
we somehow muddled through these past fifteen years.

And I guess we got settled into our routines, didn't we?
But is this what you wanted to talk about?
No. Uno-san, hypothetically speaking...

Do you think anyone could've benefited from me getting
kicked out of baseball?
What's this now? You never open up about that.

Who could've benefited? Nobody, that's who. The manager,
players, fans... None of it was good for anyone.
Even the yakuza lost out.
The yakuza?
You don't remember? Your match fixing allegations led to a crackdown on baseball gambling.
Oh, yeah...

The two families that controlled all the gambling here
couldn't keep business afloat after the crackdown.
So they pulled out of Nagoya entirely.
What two families?
Yeah, big ones from the East and West.

The Tojo Clan and the Omi Alliance? I saw their guys at
Ushijima-san's place yesterday.
Hey, if they catch on to your identity, they probably wouldn't hesitate to kill you.
It's okay. You're the only guy in Kineicho who knows my past.
I wonder why that even happened...

Everyone was just playing baseball, and suddenly there's all
this match fixing crap?
So, no leads on your end, huh?
Okay! All done!
Whew! Man, it's been forever! Feelin' light as a feather.
Well, duh. Who do you think I am?
Uno-san, you there?
Guess not. Didn't even bother to lock this place up.
If I know Uno-san, he's at the massage parlors again.
We can just wait here, then.
I'm sure he'll be back after he blows his load.
The thing is, Uno-san's too broke to be blowing any cash, too.
Never have I seen him so thirsty for his money.
Then what's he doing at a massage parlor?
When he's broke, he does a photo tour. Goes from place to place checking out all the pictures.
So there's no telling when he's gonna come back?
It'd be faster to go and find him.
Do you realize how many places there are in Kineicho?
True, but Uno-san prefers amateurs. So if we visit the places with new girls one by one, eventually we'll catch up.
You okay, Shinada!?
Thought that was it...
Yeah, seriously.
Shinada! You okay!?
Ugh. Yeah, somewhat.
You sure? Need a doctor?
I'll be fine... I think.
All right. Man! Who the hell do they think they are! Trying to kill my source of wealth!
That's what you're worried about?
Whoa, you all right!?
Probably...
What's with today? Talk about bad luck.
I want to go home.
Hey! Shinada! You alive!?
Somehow...
Are you sure? Maybe you should head to the hospital?
Haha. You're overreacting. C'mon, let's go.
Yeah, more or less.
Thought we were done for...
Yeah. The heck is going on...
Huh? Who're you? Can't just have people wandering into my kitchen...
You don't remember? Guess you wouldn't. After all, we only shared the same bench for one day. No wonder you forgot.
You're... Shinada?
So you do remember. I'm honored.

I could barely recognize ya, what with that scruffy look.
But I couldn't forget you even if I tried.
And what is that supposed to mean?
I know it ain't his extensive batting record that sticks out in your mind.
An acquaintance. Nothing to shit your pants over.
Manabe-san, I don't mean to bother you at work, but I need to ask you something.
About what? To be blunt, I'd rather ya get the hell out.
Hey now, is that how you treat a teammate you haven't seen in fifteen years?
Or is there something you don't want him finding out? Maybe... something along the lines of match fixing?
Say those words again, and I'll make sure they'll be your last.

And then he pulls out a knife. Suspicious doesn't even
begin to describe you by this point.
...Did Uno tell ya?
And ya want me to clear up what happened fifteen years ago?
Yes. But I will say, I don't believe we'd ever take part in match fixing.
And I wasn't stealing signs to begin with.
Then what do you wanna ask me?
I just need confirmation.

I want to hear it from you, a core player with the Wyverns
I knew, that there was no match fixing. That's all.
I'll tell ya. But don't go prying any deeper into this. Got it?
Not all games... were legit.
(No!)
I dunno who was sendin' instructions.
But I was gettin' texts left and right, orderin' me to steal signs and throw games.
Players who disobeyed were shuffled off the team within months.
We only kept followin' those orders so we could keep playin' in the big leagues.
I was with the team a long time, but I never heard anything like that...
You were only with the big club a day. Nobody but the starters were gettin' instructions to cheat.
Heh. You're just giving us one juicy morsel after another, eh?
Baseball's a lot like meat, y'know.
When servin' meat to customers, someone in the back has to rip out the blood, guts, and ugly shit that ain't fit to eat first.
Only after all that effort do the clean and pretty parts reach the table.
Same thing in baseball. Some things ya can't drag out into the open.
No need to, either. Nobody watchin' the game could stand the sight.
That's why it's better to keep your head down. Makes it easier to digest.
When you're eatin' good meat, no one wants to imagine a screamin' cow gettin' dragged to the slaughter.
It's better not to know. What happened behind the scenes? Just forget about it.
But baseball was my everything.
Having learned this much, how am I supposed to just bow my head and walk away?
Manabe-san, you already left the league. If the match fixing was exposed now, you couldn't be charged due to the statute of limitations.
You never thought of trying to identify the mastermind?
I thought about it, but not to the point of putting myself in danger.
Danger?
There actually was a player who tried to blow the whistle after he got traded to another team.

He must've felt guilty about throwing all those games.
Thing is, the poor guy ended up dyin' in an accident.
An accident!?

That's why ya need to give this up. Understand? We're
puttin' our necks on the line just talkin' like this.
Haven't you had a few near misses already? You must know what I'm talkin' about.
You mean those...?
Go home. Go back to your regular life.
Please, one last question! Why did you tell me all this after keeping it a secret for fifteen years?
You knew it could put you at risk, too. So why?
Simple as this. All the illicit stuff stopped after ya left the game.
That's why I thought you, out of all people, have the right to know.

I was expelled and that brought an end to the match fixing?
How the hell does that work!?
That was the last question, you said. Use your head for a minute. Then you'll realize...
If you dig any deeper into this, it's gonna be a huge mistake.
Hey, chief. You open yet?
Yeah, just about. C'mon in!
Are you sure about this?
Of course! This is your ball, after all.
I can just hit more tomorrow and the day after.
A home run ball here or there, who's gonna notice!
Don't sweat the details! This is between you and me, but...

I can't stand the type of people who pressure others to
give up what they caught, even though they wouldn't do it
themselves.
Isn't that kinda petty?
There you go. To my first official fan!
I'll do my best so you can sell that ball for good money someday.
Send this to evidence as well.
Tatsuo Shinada-san? We'd like to have a word with you. Come with us.
Do you want to fish here?
(Maybe I'll do some fishing.)
(A little fishing could be fun.)
(Time for some fishin'.)
(Think I'll take a fishing break.)
(Yay, it's fishing time!)
(Maybe now's not the time.)
(Maybe I shouldn't right now.)
(Maybe some other time.)

Select your bait, then decide where to cast your line. Each type of bait has a different range of effect, and the fish won't bite if you use the wrong bait. Items in your possession that can be used as bait will be shown in a list.
The gauge shows where the most fish are. Use bait that is effective in those areas.
Once you cast your line, wait for a fish to bite. Watch the float carefully. As soon as it bobs down, press <Action:Button_Cross@Fishing_Sea> to quickly pull your pole up.

<Action:Button_R1@Fishing_Sea> reels in, while <Action:Button_L1@Fishing_Sea> adds slack.
Pay attention to the Tension Gauge, and don't let the fish snap your line.
Use <Action:Button_LS_Left@Fishing_Sea><Action:Button_LS_Right@Fishing_Sea>, following the movement of the fish. Use <Action:Button_LS_Up@Fishing_Sea><Action:Button_LS_Down@Fishing_Sea> to raise or lower the pole.
If you control the line's tension and completely reel it in, you will successfully catch the fish.
(I bet there are lots of fish over there...)
(I bet I could catch some fish over there...)
(Bet I could catch some fish over there...)
(That looks like a good spot over there...)
(Maybe there's some fish over there...)
(Okay, now for some bait. This is what I've got here...)
(What sort of bait should I use? Hmm... This is what I've got here.)
(Now for some bait. This is what I got...)
(Okay, time to bait up. Let's see what I have here...)
(I guess I'll need some bait. Let's see what I have with me...)
